summary: The Session Report no longer states an optical-train drift verdict for a train nothing measured. Both operands of the drift subtraction now carry re-derived tiltMeasured/collimationMeasured flags: the near one from opticalTrainDiagnosticsProvider, the far one by replaying the analysis over the science rows that existed at the baseline's capturedAt. When either end lacks data the verdict is suppressed and replaced by an 'Optical Train Drift Not Measured' issue that names the axes. The executor stopped reconstructing diagnostics from a flagless snapshot and now carries the real analysis forward, so its end-of-session drift figure is only logged when both axes were measured.
root_cause: OpticalTrainBaseline (the shape persisted in session_diagnostics and held by the live pre-flight providers) is two penalty scores plus a timestamp. A penalty of 0 is simultaneously 'perfectly flat field' and 'nothing looked', so every reconstruction of an OpticalTrainDiagnostics from a snapshot landed the honesty flags on their fail-open defaults and turned 'never measured' into the best possible reading. The earlier fix added the flags to the analyzer only; nothing carried them across the snapshot boundary.
defaults_decision: Kept fail-OPEN (true) and documented why in both owned files. OpticalTrainDiagnosticsService is the one caller entitled to omit them because it always knows what it looked at; flipping the default to false would silently downgrade its own honest readings while leaving every reconstruction just as silent. The right hardening is to make them REQUIRED so omission is a compile error - that is a shared-file change, see needs_shared_change.
wiring_severed: Both tests drive the real chain. The widget test fakes only the leaf science-row streams (sessionPsfTilesProvider / sessionResidualVectorsProvider) and the persisted snapshot, then asserts on rendered dialog text; psfTilesForSessionProvider, opticalTrainDiagnosticsProvider, OpticalTrainDiagnosticsService.analyze, the reconstruction, PostSessionDiagnostics.build and the issue tiles are all real. The core test drives captureSessionStartHooksForTest/captureSessionEndHooksForTest against a real SequenceExecutor and asserts on captured log lines.

needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/preflight_providers.dart + packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/optical_train_diagnostics_service.dart + packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/preflight_rules.dart. (1) Add tiltMeasured/collimationMeasured to OpticalTrainBaseline, round-trip them in toJson/fromJson with a fail-CLOSED false default for rows written by older builds, and set them in fromDiagnostics. That removes the need for the timestamp replay this fix added to the dialog. (2) Make OpticalTrainDiagnostics.tiltMeasured/collimationMeasured and OpticalHealthScore.fromScores.isMeasured REQUIRED, so a future reconstruction that omits them is a compile error instead of a silent A grade. (3) OpticalTrainPreflightRule still subtracts two flagless OpticalTrainBaselines from the live providers and can emit 'Optical Train Has Shifted - recheck spacers, tilter, and focuser backfocus' from a placeholder 0: a night that measured collimation followed by one that did not produces a fabricated delta. Gate it on the new flags once (1) lands. I could not close (3) from my owned files: the only reachable lever was refusing to write unmeasured snapshots into opticalTrainBaselineProvider, which breaks two pinned assertions in the non-owned sequence_executor_lifecycle_test.dart and would also discard a legitimately measured tilt because collimation lacked residuals.
